claims.claim: A single-threaded hyper server usually idles at a few MB of RSS
claims.measured: rust-axum idle 1 MB; peak 3–9 MB under load
claims.why: Measured axum uses 1 MB idle and 3–9 MB under load, which is within a factor of 2 of 'a few MB'.

claims.claim: A stripped binary built with size optimization, LTO and panic=abort is typically 3–6 MB
claims.why: The measurements give container image sizes (79 MB including the base image), not the size of the stripped binary.

claims.claim: Both are well inside 20 MB and a sub-second start
claims.measured: rust-axum start-up 238 ms; memory 1 MB idle, 3–9 MB peak
claims.why: Measured start-up is about a quarter of a second and peak memory stays under 10 MB.

claims.claim: Python blows the memory budget (30–60+ MB for Python)
claims.why: Every Python server measured at 40 MB or more, which matches '30–60+ MB' and is above the 20 MB budget.
Node is about 2x the 20 MB budget even when idle.
Java measured more than 6x the 20 MB budget when idle.

claims.claim: Java blows the one-second start on an A53
claims.measured: start-up 5,939–6,224 ms on a fast x86 CPU
claims.why: Java takes about 6 s even on a fast desktop CPU, so it will take longer still on an A53.

claims.claim: Python and Node blow the one-second start on an A53
claims.measured: Python start-up 606–996 ms; Node 593–706 ms on a fast x86 CPU
claims.why: They already take 0.6–1.0 s on a much faster x86 core, so going over 1 s on an A53 is plausible once you allow for the hardware difference.

claims.claim: Go memory is feasible at roughly 10–20 MB, but it's close to the limit
claims.why: Peak memory under load measured 7–16 MB, within a factor of 2 of 10–20 MB, although idle memory (2 MB) is much lower.

claims.claim: Go binaries are 8 MB or more
claims.why: Only container image sizes (85–92 MB) were measured, not binary sizes.

claims.claim: Synchronous Rust servers (tiny_http, rouille) have the most predictable memory
claims.why: Neither tiny_http nor rouille was benchmarked.

claims.claim: C libraries (libmicrohttpd, CivetWeb, Mongoose) are small
claims.why: None of these C libraries was benchmarked; the only C++ server measured is Drogon.
